summary: The current review window was selective: quantum localization modifies transport-based femtoscopy in compact systems; an analytic finite-density thermal-photon rate removes a hard-soft cutoff ambiguity; active learning reduces an ab initio nuclear basis while preserving variational certification; and a new HENP ML review argues for physics-aware validation rather than architecture-only metrics. No new heavy-ion experiment paper met the inclusion bar.
strongest_paper: 2610.11933 - active learning saves most basis construction while preserving explicit variational certification.

papers.title: Quantum Localization Limit of Transport-Based Femtoscopy
papers.abstract: Femtoscopic correlations in proton-proton and heavy ion collisions are commonly calculated using emission sources from microscopic transport models, where emitted particles are represented as classical phase-space points. The authors replace each point with a minimum-uncertainty Gaussian phase-space distribution and find significant modifications to the proton-pair source and momentum correlation in 7 TeV pp simulations.

papers.title: Thermal photon production rate from QGP at finite density: Analytic cutoff independence
papers.abstract: The paper derives analytic cancellation of the intermediate hard-soft momentum cutoff in the thermal photon rate for a QGP with nonzero quark chemical potential, providing a finite-density generalization intended for hydrodynamic implementation.

papers.title: Active-learning construction of hyperspherical-harmonics spaces for A = 3
papers.abstract: A Gaussian-process surrogate and cost-aware acquisition rule select extensions of a hyperspherical-harmonics basis. Every accepted extension is explicitly solved, and the method reproduces uniform K=60 energies within 4 keV while leaving more than 60% of that space unbuilt.

papers.title: Machine Learning Meets High-Energy Nuclear Physics: From Pattern Recognition to Physics-Integrated Discovery
papers.abstract: A mini-review surveys physics-integrated ML workflows in heavy-ion, neutron-star, lattice, and QCD research, emphasizing physical constraints, uncertainty quantification, and validation.

papers.title: A Density Functional for Quark Matter with Screened Confinement Interactions
papers.abstract: The paper derives a quark-matter density functional from a screened linear-confinement ansatz and proposes identifying the screening parameter with the Fermi momentum. The construction is potentially relevant to dense-matter equations of state but requires broader validation.
